doc: Submits a job. Idempotent on the job id: the same id with the same job (every field but the priority) answers from the job already made, in whatever state it is now, so a retry after a lost answer never runs the work twice. The job is recorded as queued before the answer; the call never waits for placement. A refusal records nothing.

flags.doc: The job's id: 1 to 63 bytes of letters, digits, dot, underscore and dash (design section 5.3; the service checks it). Submitting the same id with the same job (every field but the priority) answers from the job already made; the same id with a different job is refused job-id-conflict. Empty: the service mints one, so a submit without an id that is repeated after a lost answer makes a second job.
flags.name: id

flags.doc: The image, pinned by digest: NAME@sha256:HEX, with an optional tag after the name. The service rejects an image without a digest.
flags.name: spec.image

flags.doc: The program to run. Empty: the image's default. How it combines with the image's own entrypoint and command is set by the server that implements SubmitJob.
flags.name: spec.command

flags.doc: The arguments the program is started with, in order.
flags.name: spec.args

flags.doc: The environment of the job, by variable name.
flags.name: spec.env

flags.doc: CPU, in thousandths of a core.
flags.name: spec.needs.cpu-millis

flags.doc: Memory, in bytes.
flags.name: spec.needs.memory-bytes

flags.doc: Scratch disk, in bytes. Absent: none is asked for.
flags.name: spec.needs.disk-bytes

flags.doc: The number of GPUs. 0: none. A job that sets only gpus and gpu_class, and no Constraints.accelerator, keeps the meaning it has always had: the class is read through the alias table of design section 3.8, so a full spelling pins its variant and a family name such as nvidia-a100 matches every variant of it.
flags.name: spec.needs.gpus

flags.doc: The GPU class, in the spelling the agent reports: the lower-case model name with its words joined by dashes, such as nvidia-a100-sxm4-80gb. Empty: any class. It is resolved through the alias table like Accelerator.model.
flags.name: spec.needs.gpu-class

flags.doc: The job needs the whole host: it is placed only on a host that holds no other job, and a host is drained for it (design section 5.4). The other needs still bound which hosts are capable.
flags.name: spec.needs.whole-host

flags.doc: The operating system: linux or macos. Empty: any.
flags.name: spec.constraints.os

flags.doc: The CPU architecture: x86_64 or arm64. aarch64 is accepted and stored as arm64 (design section 3.8). Empty: any.
flags.name: spec.constraints.arch

flags.doc: The mode the host runs jobs in. Unspecified: either.
flags.name: spec.constraints.exec

flags.doc: The least instruction-set level, in request syntax such as x86-64-v3 or armv8.2-a. A host is capable when it reports that level or a higher one of the same architecture. Empty: any.
flags.name: spec.constraints.isa-level

flags.doc: The vendor, such as nvidia.
flags.name: spec.constraints.accelerator.vendor

flags.doc: The model: a family such as nvidia-a100, or a full spelling such as nvidia-a100-sxm4-80gb.
flags.name: spec.constraints.accelerator.model

flags.doc: The least number of devices.
flags.name: spec.constraints.accelerator.count

flags.doc: The least memory of each device, in whole GiB.
flags.name: spec.constraints.accelerator.memory-per-device-gib

flags.doc: The least interconnect, as kind>=size.
flags.name: spec.constraints.accelerator.interconnect

flags.doc: The form factor: sxm or pcie.
flags.name: spec.constraints.accelerator.form-factor

flags.doc: The most seconds the job may run, counted from running. The service refuses a job without one (absent or 0, wall-time-not-positive) and one above its ceiling (wall-time-above-ceiling).
flags.name: spec.wall-limit-seconds

flags.doc: What the job may reach over the network. Unspecified: none.
flags.name: spec.network

flags.doc: The host ports forwarded to the job. Empty: none, and no inbound path to the job.
flags.name: spec.ports-file

flags.doc: The files the host writes for the job before it starts.
flags.name: spec.files-file

flags.doc: The job's priority among queued jobs. 0 when not given. A resubmit that differs from the job already made only in its priority is the same job (design section 5.3).
flags.name: spec.priority

flags.doc: The client's labels, by key. A listing can filter by them.
flags.name: spec.labels

doc: Reads a job: its state, its host once placed, its times and its host's silence. Changes nothing.

flags.doc: The id of the job to read.
flags.name: job-id

doc: Lists jobs by state, label, client and the time they were queued, a page at a time. Changes nothing.

flags.doc: Only jobs in one of these states. Empty: every state.
flags.name: states

flags.doc: Only jobs that carry every one of these labels with the same value. Empty: any labels.
flags.name: labels

flags.doc: Only jobs queued at or after this time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
flags.name: queued-after-ms

flags.doc: Only jobs queued before this time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
flags.name: queued-before-ms

flags.doc: Only jobs submitted by the client of this name (Job.client). Absent: every client's.
flags.name: client

flags.doc: The most jobs in one answer. 0: the server's own page size. A server may answer fewer.
flags.name: page-size

flags.doc: Where to continue: the next page token of the previous answer of the same listing. Empty: the first page.
flags.name: page-token

doc: Cancels a job. Idempotent on the job: cancelling twice is the same as once. A queued job is cancelled at once; a placed, starting or running job is asked to stop and is cancelled when its host reports it stopped; an ended job is unchanged.

flags.doc: The id of the job to cancel.
flags.name: job-id

doc: Reads the result of an ended job, for the retention window after it ended. A job that has not ended has no result, and the call is refused. Changes nothing.

flags.doc: The id of the ended job whose result to read.
flags.name: job-id

doc: Reads the log tail held so far, also for a running job, and for the retention window after the job ended. Changes nothing.

flags.doc: The id of the job whose log tail to read.
flags.name: job-id

doc: Lists the hosts, each with the resources booked on it. Changes nothing.
Takes a host out of placement for a time, or extends a cordon already there. A cordon lapses unless it is extended. Jobs already on the host go on.

flags.doc: The id of the host to cordon.
flags.name: host-id

flags.doc: How long the cordon holds unless it is extended, in seconds from the call. Absent: 300. The server cuts a longer one to 3600.
flags.name: cordon-secs

doc: Lifts a host's cordon. Lifting a host that is not cordoned changes nothing.

flags.doc: The id of the host whose cordon to lift.
flags.name: host-id

doc: Lists the machine providers. Changes nothing.
Lists the ended bookings, a page at a time. Changes nothing.

flags.doc: Only records of bookings that ended at or after this time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
flags.name: from-ms

flags.doc: Only records of bookings that ended before this time, in milliseconds since the Unix epoch.
flags.name: to-ms

flags.doc: Only records of this host. Empty: every host.
flags.name: host-id

flags.doc: Only records of this job. Empty: every job.
flags.name: job-id

flags.doc: The most records in one answer. 0: the server's own page size. A server may answer fewer.
flags.name: page-size

flags.doc: Where to continue: the next page token of the previous answer of the same listing. Empty: the first page.
flags.name: page-token
